about: Input to scripts/images/prepare-photos.py. Every photo the site ships, where it came from, how it is cut, and what the privacy and accuracy review found. Sources are Kelvin's Drive folder 'website pictures' (zip of 4 Oct 2026), kept in the git-ignored media-inbox/drive/. Kelvin confirmed on 4 Oct 2026 that every photo is Nebsam's to publish and that anyone recognisable agreed to appear. 'origin' is what the image is, so a reader of this file never mistakes an illustration for a photograph: photograph (taken of a real place), manufacturer (the maker's or Nebsam's product shot), ai-generated (gap-fill under brief 3.6: never Nebsam staff, premises, vehicles or platform).

copied.from: the old site's public/images/main-entrance.jpeg, unchanged (1280x720, no EXIF); used since Sprint 12m, moved here in 12n
copied.review: The Mombasa branch entrance, Makupa. Kelvin, 4 Oct 2026: the old site's premises set is the Mombasa branch. Nobody in frame; the truck's plate is not visible. NOT made by the script, so a re-run never touches it.

photos.src: Solutions/Vehicle tracking/Coastal Fleet Tracking in Mombasa.png
photos.review: Panel van on a coastal road. The box leaves out the mock 'Fleet Tracking' phone screen on the right, which would read as the Nebsam app (brief 3.6: AI never depicts the platform). Its leader line, which would now point at nothing, is healed out. The map pin over the van stays: it is a symbol, not data. Blank plate.

The Nairobi HQ, Kiambu Road. Three people in frame, each about 30px tall at full size, side-on or from behind: not identifiable. The car's rear plate and the motorbike's plate are blurred. The box trims the gravel foreground: it was most of the frame, and fine texture is what costs bytes on a branch card (Contact LCP, 12n).

The original is two photos side by side; the box keeps the shopfront. No people. The fascia sign prints 0769 063 333, which lib/company.ts gives as a Mombasa number, while the Nakuru card lists +254 725 221122 (register V89). The posters print 0759 000 111, the published WhatsApp number.

photos.src: Solutions/Vehicle tracking/Coastal Fleet Tracking in Mombasa.png
photos.review: The same source as home-solutions, cut for the solution page band: the mock phone screen is boxed out and its leader line healed out; the map pin over the van stays as a symbol. 3:2 rather than 21:9, because the van fills the height of what is left once the phone is cut away.

Two depot workers on radios, trucks behind. Kept by Kelvin (not among the seven left out). The laptop screen showed a fleet map that could read as the Nebsam platform (brief 3.6), so it is blurred. The cap carries a small white mark too small to read; no Nebsam branding anywhere.

photos.src: Solutions/Fuel monitoring/Technician Installing Truck Fuel Sensor.png
photos.review: Left out in 12n, reused at Kelvin's instruction (5 Oct 2026, V90). A technician fitting a fuel level sensor to a truck's tank. The source prints 'nebsam Digital Solutions' on his back, which would present an AI figure as Nebsam staff (brief 3.6, PART 18), so the box cuts the frame just right of the lettering: what is left carries no Nebsam branding. The tracker on the chassis is labelled 'FMB', a real device family's name, so that label is blurred. The laptop is cut away with the left of the frame.

photos.src: Solutions/Vehicle security/Technician Wiring a Car Dashboard.png
photos.review: Left out in 12n, reused at Kelvin's instruction (5 Oct 2026, V90). A technician wiring behind a car's dashboard. As with fuel monitoring, the shirt reads 'nebsam Digital Solutions', so the box cuts the frame right of the lettering and the AI figure carries no Nebsam branding. The workshop has no signage. The hand holding a key fob is cut away with the left of the frame. Vehicle makers' badges stay: they name the car, not a relationship.

Left out in 12n, reused at Kelvin's instruction (5 Oct 2026, V90). A technician with a key-programming tablet and a remote key beside an open car door. No Nebsam branding and no signage. The source's left third is a blank blue fade made for text, and text never sits on a photo here, so the box cuts it away. The tablet shows a generic programming checklist, not the Nebsam platform.

Left out in 12n, reused at Kelvin's instruction (5 Oct 2026, V90). A PSV minibus on a highway. The box cuts away the traffic police officer waving it down and the roadside government sign, which would imply police ties. The 'Mombasa Express' livery, which may be a real operator's name, is filled out of the bonnet paint (two boxes, so the stripes and the bonnet edge survive). Blurred: the realistic plate (KDG 742X), and a windscreen sticker reading 'Speed governor certified', which would read as a certification nobody has documented; it stays a sticker, unreadable. The route boards (Mombasa, Nairobi) and the PSV sign stay.

Left out in 12n, reused at Kelvin's instruction (5 Oct 2026, V90). The source is a diptych: a truck on a highway at dusk, and an invented control room whose screens would read as the Nebsam platform, staffed by AI figures who would read as Nebsam staff (brief 3.6). Only the truck half is used. The box also cuts away the arc of icons over it. The ring marking the cab camera stays, with the start of its signal line: a symbol, like the map pin over the van on vehicle tracking. No plate, no livery. The portrait crop is only 508 px wide, because the source is 941 px tall.
A pickup and a tractor on a farm, workers in the fields. Blank plate, no farm or company name.

A row of rental cars and an attendant with a tablet. The box cuts away a mock "Fleet Online / Location Tracking / Geofence" panel drawn on the building and its map pin: it read as the Nebsam platform (brief 3.6).

photos.review: A container truck on a road with a geofence boundary drawn around an industrial area. The box cuts away a fleet dashboard, a phone and a list of realistic Kenyan-format plates (KBL 345X, KCN 902Z) that could belong to real vehicles.

A parked 4x4 with a lock symbol and a ring drawn under it. The box cuts away the man holding a phone with a mock "Immobilised" app screen; the floating "Vehicle immobilised" panel is blurred (a mock app panel, and its "Recovery support" line is a claim the article does not make).
